exceptions.reason: Text past its reader, at one test site: this integration test writes two package.json files into its own scratch monorepo, the boundary that uses JSON. eslintVersion serialises node_modules/eslint/package.json for the ESLint line under test, and lintScript serialises the root package.json for the lint command under test; each is JSON.stringify of a written-out object, the form preferred over hand-written JSON text. This record authorises those two writes for this symptom alone and grants no other test-body logic in the file.

whys.because: monorepoRun overlays two package.json files onto a fixture repository through overlaidFileText, and a package.json file is JSON text on disk, so each object the test writes must be serialised there.
whys.evidence: src/infrastructure/engines/eslint/runner/native-exceptions/native-exceptions.integration.test.ts:537 eslintVersion and :539 lintScript; monorepoRun's overlaidFileText files map writes ${repo}/node_modules/eslint/package.json and ${repo}/package.json.

whys.why: Why does monorepoRun overlay package.json files onto the fixture repository?
whys.because: The ESLint runner under test reads the installed eslint version and each lint script from package.json files, and the test proves its native-exception reports for each ESLint line and each lint command, so the values vary per case and belong to the test's subject.
whys.evidence: src/infrastructure/engines/eslint/runner/embedded-runner/create-eslint-runner.ts packageJsonExceptions and scannedPackageExceptions; the monorepoRun cases in the same test file pass version and lintCommand per row.

whys.why: Why does the ESLint runner read the eslint version and the lint scripts from package.json files?
whys.because: ESLint's installed major decides how the runner finds the config and reads its flags, and npm installs that version in node_modules/eslint/package.json and keeps each lint command in a package's scripts, so package.json is where both facts live.
whys.evidence: src/infrastructure/engines/eslint/runner/config-roots/config-lookup.ts:53 installedEslintMajor reads node_modules/eslint/package.json through eslintVersionFileSchema; :73 scriptsOf reads a package.json's scripts through packageJsonSchema.

whys.why: Why does ESLint's installed major decide how the runner finds the config and reads its flags?
whys.because: ESLint 9 resolves one eslint.config file from the repository root unless a lint script passes the v10_config_lookup_from_file flag, while other majors resolve the nearest config to each linted file, so the runner must match that lookup to judge which config applies to each file.
whys.evidence: src/infrastructure/engines/eslint/runner/config-roots/config-lookup.ts:18 ROOT_LOOKUP_MAJOR is 9, :30 NEAREST_LOOKUP_FLAGS, :116 detectedLookup chooses nearest-to-file or repository-root.

whys.why: Why must the runner judge which config applies to each linted file?
whys.because: A folder's own config can leave out the projection or override a rule for the files it governs, which is a weakening Hone must report as a native exception, so a wrong lookup would hide an override or invent one.
whys.evidence: docs/extending.md:174: a package config that leaves the projection out lists each of its files under unrecorded as config-override; ADOPTING.md step 4a.

whyChain.rootCause: ESLint lets each folder's config override a rule or leave out the projection, and which config governs a file depends on facts npm keeps in package.json files, which are JSON.
whyChain.rootCheck: On 2026-11-20, self-check listed exactly two CD-27#test-body-logic findings in this file, at 537:73 and 539:70, both JSON.stringify writes into the overlaid scratch package.json files.
whyChain.readback: ESLint lets each folder's config override a rule, and which config governs a file depends on package.json facts, therefore the runner judges the config lookup from the eslint version and lint scripts, therefore the native-exceptions integration test writes those package.json files into its scratch monorepo, therefore it calls JSON.stringify on two written-out objects.
